stories.title: The sexy AI-powered dating app scams are here
stories.simple_summary: Scammers are creating fake dating apps that use AI to pretend to be real people and trick users into sending money. A security expert found one of these apps and was contacted by a fake profile.
stories.why_it_matters: Be careful on dating apps — if someone you just met asks for money or to move to a secret payment system, they're probably not real. Check if the app is from a trusted company.

stories.title: A brief history of AI executives calling for regulation
stories.simple_summary: Big AI company leaders like Sam Altman from OpenAI are publicly saying AI should be regulated and slowed down, even though they profit from AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important for investors and policy makers — it doesn't change how you use AI today, but shows disagreement among tech leaders about safety.

stories.title: Allowing AI firms to collude to ‘pace the frontier’ is a dangerous proposition
stories.simple_summary: An article warns that letting AI companies work together to 'slow down' progress could be risky and unfair.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a debate for lawmakers and investors — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: Amazon launches Alexa+ in India with Hindi support
stories.simple_summary: Amazon's voice assistant Alexa is now available in India and can understand and respond in Hindi, the most widely spoken language there.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in India and speak Hindi, you can now use Alexa without switching to English — but if you're elsewhere, this doesn't affect you.

stories.title: Gates Foundation commits $1 billion to improving global AI access
stories.simple_summary: The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation announced they're spending 1 billion dollars to help poor countries and communities get better access to AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This won't change your daily life, but it means AI development might focus more on helping people in developing countries solve real problems.

stories.title: Poll: Americans say there’s a serious risk of AI destroying humanity
stories.simple_summary: A poll asked Americans if they're worried AI could destroy humanity, and many said yes, they think it's a serious risk.
stories.why_it_matters: Many people are nervous about AI safety, but this is a general worry rather than a specific threat you need to prepare for today.

stories.title: Why Trump is all-in on AI despite the warnings
stories.simple_summary: Former President Trump is supporting AI development heavily even though many people warn it could be dangerous.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a political story — it shows disagreement among leaders about whether AI should be developed quickly or carefully.

stories.title: Bipartisan, big tech push for AI regulation comes as Trump claims 'hoax'
stories.simple_summary: Democrats and Republicans, along with big tech companies, are pushing for AI regulation rules, but Trump says these worries are a hoax.
stories.why_it_matters: Political leaders disagree about whether AI needs strict rules — this is a Washington debate that won't change how you use AI yet.

stories.title: Why the US and China are at odds on AI threats
stories.simple_summary: The United States and China disagree about what dangers AI poses and how to handle them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly about geopolitics and international relations — it doesn't directly affect how you use AI in your daily life.

stories.title: We don’t need AI regulation — leave safety to us, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says
stories.simple_summary: Jensen Huang, the leader of Nvidia (a company that makes chips for AI), says AI is just normal technology and doesn't need government regulation — companies should police themselves.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly important to investors and policymakers — it shows one side of the debate about whether AI companies should regulate themselves or if governments should step in.

stories.title: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
stories.simple_summary: Polls show most Americans don't want AI data centers (the huge buildings that power AI) built in their areas. 61 percent of people surveyed said they oppose building them.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live near where a data center might be built, this shows your neighbors probably don't want it — these centers use lots of power and water and can affect local communities.

stories.title: Trump Defended A.I. Data Centers on Truth Social, and Commenters Clapped Back
stories.simple_summary: Trump posted support for AI data centers on his social media, but people commented disagreeing with him.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a political story showing public disagreement about whether AI data centers should be built — it reflects the divide shown in the previous poll.
